$comment: Pacific Carpentry admin API + data contract. REST-style endpoints (implement as Next.js Route Handlers under app/api/admin/* or as Server Actions). All admin routes require authentication. Money is AED, stored as whole-dirham integers. All product/project records are bilingual (en/ar).

currency.note: Prices are whole dirhams stored as Int. Switch to fils (Int cents) if you need decimals.

auth.suggestion: NextAuth (Auth.js) credential or email provider, or Supabase Auth. Single 'owner'/'staff' role to start.

Product.category: enum: dining-tables | chairs | cabinets | doors | shelving

Order.status: enum: pending | paid | in_production | shipped | completed | cancelled

auth.$note: Prefer NextAuth (Auth.js) or Supabase Auth over hand-rolling. The endpoints below describe the behavior the login screen needs; a library will provide equivalents.

POST /api/auth/login.desc: Authenticate a staff user and start a session.
POST /api/auth/login.onSuccess: Set an httpOnly session cookie, then redirect to /admin (Dashboard).
POST /api/auth/login.onError: 401 with { error: 'Invalid credentials' } shown inline on the form.

POST /api/auth/logout.desc: End the session (triggered by the sidebar Sign out button).
POST /api/auth/logout.onSuccess: Clear the session cookie, redirect to /admin/login.

guard.desc: Every /admin page and /api/admin/* handler must verify the session.
guard.suggestion: Next.js middleware matching '/admin/:path*' (excluding /admin/login) + a server-side session check in the admin layout; redirect unauthenticated users to /admin/login.
guard.roles: Single 'owner'/'staff' role is enough to start; model a role field for future granularity.

GET /api/admin/dashboard.desc: Aggregated KPIs + recent activity for the dashboard.

kpis.revenue30d: int (sum of order.total in last 30 days)

response.recentOrders: Order[] (latest 5, minimal fields: number, fullName, createdAt, status, total)
response.topProducts: [{ productId, nameEn, unitsSold, revenue }] (computed from OrderItem)

GET /api/admin/products.response: Product[] (include colors + sizes so the table can show swatches and price range)

GET /api/admin/products/:id.desc: Single product with colors + sizes for the editor.

POST /api/admin/products.desc: Create a product with its finishes and sizes.
POST /api/admin/products.validation: Zod: >=1 color, >=1 size, every price is a positive integer, hex matches /^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$/, slug unique.

PUT /api/admin/products/:id.desc: Update a product. Replace colors/sizes arrays wholesale (diff by id; create new rows without id, delete removed ones).
PUT /api/admin/products/:id.body: same shape as POST, with colors[].id / sizes[].id present for existing rows

derived.priceRange: min..max of sizes[].price — shown in list and editor summary

query.status: all | pending | paid | in_production | shipped | completed (optional)

GET /api/admin/orders.response: Order[] (number, fullName, email, createdAt, itemCount, status, total)

PATCH /api/admin/orders/:id/status.desc: Update order status from the detail stepper.
PATCH /api/admin/orders/:id/status.note: Bump updatedAt; optionally write a status-history row for audit.

POST /api/admin/projects.body: { slug, titleEn, titleAr, catEn, catAr, year, images }

messages.$note: The storefront contact form POSTs to a public endpoint (e.g. POST /api/contact) that creates a Message with read=false.

POST /api/admin/upload.desc: Upload an image, return its public URL to append to a product/project images[].

mapping.PRODUCTS[] -> Product + ProductColor + P: product.name.{en,ar} -> nameEn/nameAr; product.tagline -> taglineEn/Ar; product.desc -> descEn/Ar; product.cat -> category; product.colors[].{en,ar,hex} -> ProductColor; product.sizes[].{en,ar,price} -> ProductSize.{labelEn,labelAr,price}
mapping.PROJECTS[] -> Project: project.{en,ar} -> titleEn/titleAr; project.cat.{en,ar} -> catEn/catAr; project.year -> year
mapping.T -> messages/en.json + ar.json: storefront i18n strings (not needed for admin chrome, which is English-only)
